name: Brian Scott
contest: Board of County Commissioners, District 2 – At Large
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Scott is the incumbent (first elected 2022, flipping the seat from Democrat Pat Gerard), served as commission chair in 2025, holds roughly a 4.5-to-1 fundraising edge, and has the Tampa Bay Times recommendation; Hughes entered late (qualified June 2026). Countywide Pinellas races have leaned Republican since 2022.
raised: $199,089 raised incl. $10,000 in-kind; $177,654 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Business and transportation industry donors; his political committee reportedly received an additional $35,000 (Tampa Bay Times/Yahoo, June 2026); Pinellas County Republican Party
lgbtqDetails: Per Axios Tampa Bay (June 18, 2026), Scott was one of only three commissioners who said they supported a Pride Month proclamation that failed for lack of a supermajority; he also signed the board's unanimous 'Faith and Family Month' proclamation that LGBTQ+ advocates criticized (St. Pete Catalyst, WFLA, June 2026). No Equality Florida or Moms for Liberty rating found.
platform: President of Escot Bus Lines and past president of TRAX Insurance; former PSTA board member, Forward Pinellas vice chair. Campaign emphasizes cutting the property tax rate (says the county cut millage 4 of the last 5 years), storm resilience after Helene and Milton (led the $813M People First relief program and $125.7M beach renourishment as chair), developer-funded infrastructure, and the 2025 PSTA network redesign. Open to a voter referendum on TIF commitments over $100M (LWV guide).
controversy: None significant reported. Searches of Tampa Bay Times, Florida Politics and local outlets found no ethics or conflict-of-interest reporting involving his bus company.
endorsements: Tampa Bay Times editorial board (Oct 1, 2026), Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate
primaryResult: n/a (no primary; single candidate per party)

name: Tim Hughes
contest: Board of County Commissioners, District 2 – At Large
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Hughes is a first-time candidate who qualified in June 2026 with no fundraising reported at that point; he trails the incumbent roughly 4.5-to-1 in money and the Tampa Bay Times called him a 'relative newcomer.' Countywide Pinellas contests have favored Republicans since 2022.
raised: $43,331 raised; $25,707 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Pinellas County Democratic Party; environmental/Sierra Club network (he is Suncoast Sierra Club conservation chair); small-dollar donors
lgbtqDetails: No LGBTQ+-specific statements, votes or endorsements found; Pinellas County Democratic Party endorsement only (Blue Voter Guide).
platform: Retired environmental specialist with about 20 years in watershed/floodplain management for Prince William County, Va., public works; Suncoast Sierra Club 2025 volunteer of the year and 2026 conservation chair; serves on Clearwater's Community Resiliency board. Priorities: countywide stormwater GIS mapping and FEMA CRS flood-premium discounts, protecting parks and green space, converting aging mobile home parks into resilient affordable condos using SHIP/SAIL/Sadowski funds, right-sizing PSTA with mini-buses and longer hours, and pursuing regional rail. Supports a referendum for TIF commitments over $100M.
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Creative Loafing Tampa, Voter Action Pinellas (listed as Democrat on your ballot)
primaryResult: n/a (no primary; single candidate per party)

name: Kathleen Peters
contest: Board of County Commissioners, District 6 – Single Member
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Peters is a two-term incumbent who was re-elected without opposition in 2022, is seeking a third term, holds a roughly 12-to-1 fundraising edge over Glenn, and has the Tampa Bay Times recommendation. District 6 (south Pinellas beaches/Seminole area) is a Republican-leaning single-member district.
raised: $189,964 raised incl. $10,000 in-kind; $140,876 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Business, real-estate and health-care donors (Florida Politics reported $63,650 raised within months of her April 2025 filing); Pinellas County Republican Party
lgbtqDetails: Axios Tampa Bay (June 18, 2026) reported Peters 'has previously supported Pride measures' and said she had no issue with the substance of the 2026 Pride proclamation but noted no local organizations had requested it; the proclamation failed. She signed the board's unanimous 'Faith and Family Month' proclamation that LGBTQ+ advocates criticized (WFLA, St. Pete Catalyst). No Equality Florida or Moms for Liberty rating found.
platform: Former South Pasadena commissioner and mayor, six years in the Florida House (2012–2018), county commissioner since 2018/2019. Tampa Bay Times describes her as fiscally constrained but pragmatic; she championed behavioral-health and addiction programs (Care About Me), wants to keep lowering the property tax rate, and wants the state to stop preempting local control over issues like short-term rentals. Campaign site lists behavioral health reform, public safety and fiscal responsibility, and environmental protection/infrastructure. She declined to answer the League of Women Voters questionnaire.
controversy: None involving Peters herself. Tampa Bay Times (Oct 12, 2026) reported that Pinellas sheriff's deputies checked on her opponent David Glenn Jr. over '#86Peters' hashtags and an Oct. 4 '86 Peters' seashell photo; Peters said she did not file the report.
endorsements: Tampa Bay Times editorial board (Oct 1, 2026), Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate
primaryResult: n/a (no primary; single candidate per party)

name: David Glenn Jr.
contest: Board of County Commissioners, District 6 – Single Member
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Glenn is a first-time candidate and Democratic precinct committee person challenging a two-term incumbent in a Republican-leaning single-member district, with roughly one-twelfth of her fundraising. The Tampa Bay Times said he 'has some good ideas' but recommended Peters.
raised: $15,105 raised; $12,911 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County, Florida NOW, Democratic Veterans Caucus of Florida; small-dollar donors
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by the Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County (per Sway.co endorsement listing, 2026); Sway tags his endorsers with LGBTQ-rights and reproductive-rights movements. No public statements on LGBTQ+ policy found.
platform: Licensed Florida architect and interior designer (FAMU B.Arch, USF M.Arch), registered in nine other states; former PSTA Transit Advisory Committee member. Argues Pinellas has little open land left so growth should go vertical in select areas to grow the tax base while protecting low-density neighborhoods; wants workforce/affordable housing, more tourism revenue, more transit routes and frequency plus commuter rail planning, and funding for libraries and parks. Opposes TIF referendums ('let the elected leaders make the hard decisions') and says the current commission is 'attempting to dismantle' transit.
controversy: Tampa Bay Times (Oct 12, 2026) reported Pinellas sheriff's deputies visited his home and called him months earlier after a report about his '#86Peters' Facebook hashtags, and that an Oct. 4 post of seashells spelling '86 Peters' prompted another law-enforcement inquiry with no further action. Glenn said 'It was just a hashtag' and not a threat; Peters said she did not file the report.
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County, Florida NOW, Democratic Veterans Caucus of Florida, Creative Loafing Tampa
primaryResult: n/a (no primary; single candidate per party)

name: Curtis Campogni
contest: School Board Member, District 3 – At Large
pollingDetails: No public poll. In the Aug. 18, 2026 three-way primary Peters led 36.3% to Campogni's 34.8% (Dawn Douglas, a Democrat, took 28.8%), a gap of under 2,000 votes out of roughly 165,000. Campogni, a registered NPA, has out-raised the incumbent since the primary and picked up the Tampa Bay Times, teachers union and Realtors endorsements; Douglas's Democratic-leaning voters are the swing bloc in the runoff.
raised: $29,240 raised incl. $5,783 in-kind; $18,948 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Pinellas Classroom Teachers Association / PESPA (PCTA-PESPA), Suncoast Tampa Association of Realtors, Amplify Clearwater PAC (Clearwater chamber), small-dollar donors
lgbtqDetails: No LGBTQ+-specific statements or endorsements found. On book challenges he told the LWV the current process 'allows parents to make choices for their own children while ensuring one household does not make decisions for every other family' and said he 'will not be drawn into ideological battles.' Voter Action Pinellas (Democratic-aligned) says he 'indicates alignment with our values.'
platform: 42-year-old Safety Harbor father of two Pinellas students adopted from foster care; 15+ years working with at-risk youth as a group-home worker, case manager and program director; founder of Speak4MC training firm; vice chair of DJJ Circuit 6 Advisory Board. Slogan 'Put a Dad on the School Board.' Priorities: teacher pay and retention ('hear them, empower them, pay them'), reversing enrollment decline, community partnerships, campus safety and discipline, and pushing back on the administration rather than rubber-stamping; questioned the Sexton Elementary closure recommendation and called for more transparency. Supports the district property-tax referendum for employee pay and income limits on vouchers.
endorsements: Tampa Bay Times editorial board (Oct 1, 2026), Pinellas Classroom Teachers Association (PCTA-PESPA), Suncoast Tampa Association of Realtors, Amplify Clearwater PAC, Creative Loafing Tampa, Voter Action Pinellas
primaryResult: advanced from Aug 18 primary with 34.8% (2nd) behind Dawn Peters 36.3%; Dawn Douglas 28.8% eliminated

name: Dawn Peters
contest: School Board Member, District 3 – At Large
pollingDetails: No public poll. Peters finished first in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary with 36.3% (59,783 votes in the WTSP preliminary count) to Campogni's 34.8%, with Democrat Dawn Douglas at 28.8%. She entered the runoff with about $1,400 cash on hand (Florida Politics), has been out-raised since, and is a registered Republican in a nonpartisan countywide race where Douglas's voters decide the outcome.
raised: $21,925 raised incl. $5,000 in-kind; $14,143 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, latest report as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Pinellas County Republican Party; Republican officeholders (Reps. Kim Berfield, Linda Chaney, Berny Jacques; Commissioners Kathleen Peters, Brian Scott, Vince Nowicki); has said she is avoiding political-committee money this cycle (Florida Politics, Oct 2026)
lgbtqDetails: Elected in 2022 with Moms for Liberty Pinellas and DeSantis-aligned backing on a parental-rights platform; the Tampa Bay Times (Oct 2026) reports she 'helped lead the effort to remove books from school libraries' and was once a strong supporter of DeSantis's parental-rights initiatives, though she has since called state book-removal efforts a 'distraction' and softened her rhetoric. Florida Politics (Oct 2026) reports she says Moms for Liberty is not backing her in 2026 and she did not seek its endorsement, while her campaign website still listed the Moms for Liberty Pinellas Chapter among endorsements. No 1776 Project PAC involvement in the 2026 race was found.
platform: Personal trainer, former PTA president and Thurgood Marshall Fundamental Middle volunteer coordinator; elected 2022, now board vice chair. Pushed to livestream public comment and post workshop recordings; opposed the district tax rate; backed cellphone bans and the employee-pay property-tax referendum; now opposes universal vouchers without income limits and says private schools taking vouchers should meet the same accountability standards. Priorities: continuing academic growth, 'stability' amid state and federal uncertainty, raising teacher and staff pay, and career/technical and military pathways. On the seven-school closure plan she says every child will be offered 'something at least as good' and urges residents to attend town halls.
controversy: Tampa Bay Times (Oct 19 and 26, 2022) reported 2020 social-media screenshots in which Peters appeared to take the 'QAnon oath,' posted a photo of her partner taking 'the oath,' referred to the 2020 election as 'Trump 2Q2Q,' and retweeted a post calling the moon landing, 9/11 and the pandemic 'three major hoaxes'; asked whether she believed them she said 'I have no idea,' then revised her answer to say she does not follow QAnon. The Times editorial board (Oct 27, 2022) said she was not fit for the board; its Oct 2026 recommendation revisits the episode and says she has since softened some stances. TBN Weekly also covered the 2022 QAnon dispute.
endorsements: Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate; Clerk Ken Burke, Tax Collector Adam Ross, Property Appraiser Mike Twitty; Clearwater Mayor Bruce Rector; Reps. Kim Berfield, Linda Chaney, Berny Jacques; Commissioners Kathleen Peters, Brian Scott, Vince Nowicki; board member Eileen Long; former board member Carol Cook
primaryResult: led Aug 18 primary with 36.3% over Curtis Campogni 34.8% and Dawn Douglas 28.8%; forced to runoff (no majority)

name: Jim Downes
contest: East Lake Tarpon Special Fire Control District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Downes is the sitting Seat 2 commissioner (term 2023–2026, GoodParty.org) and is on the Pinellas GOP slate; Voter Action Pinellas lists him as a registered Republican. His challenger has no website or published platform. Information on this race is thin.
raised: $0 raised, $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat.
platform: FSU business graduate, 23 years at Honeywell, 16 years owning an industrial construction company, 4 years as East Lake fire commissioner. Told the LWV the top issue is potential revenue loss from Amendment 3; the board is reviewing postponed capital purchases, a hiring freeze and reassigning staff duties while protecting mutual-aid service to neighboring communities. Says the district replaces bunker gear early and trains with forestry and county disaster services.
endorsements: Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate (nonpartisan seat)

name: Bob Fornwalt
contest: East Lake Tarpon Special Fire Control District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Fornwalt is challenging a four-year incumbent, has no campaign website and declined every LWV questionnaire question, but has self-funded or raised $8,000 and spent $8,542. Voter Action Pinellas lists him as No Party Affiliation. Information is thin.
raised: $8,000 raised; $8,542 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat.
platform: Tarpon Springs resident; LWV guide lists 'some college' and professional experience as 'underground fire license' (likely underground fire-line contractor). Declined to respond to all League of Women Voters questions; Activate Pinellas found no published background or platform.

name: Benjamin Nichols
contest: Palm Harbor Special Fire Control and Rescue District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Nichols is challenging an incumbent who has the firefighters union endorsement and the Pinellas GOP slate spot; he has reported only $1,604 in in-kind contributions. Information is thin.
raised: $1,604 in-kind only; $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat.
platform: Palm Harbor entrepreneur and business owner; president of the Palm Harbor Merchants Association, vice president of Palm Harbor Main Street, Palm Harbor Chamber member (LWV guide; Palm Harbor/Dunedin Beacon calls him a 'business owner and civic leader'). Says he would bring budgeting and accountability experience, evaluate Amendment 3's revenue impact with district leadership, review emergency plans and coordination with neighboring agencies, and listen to firefighters on equipment needs.

name: Julie Peluso
contest: Palm Harbor Special Fire Control and Rescue District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Peluso is the incumbent Seat 2 commissioner (term 2023–2026), endorsed by the Palm Harbor & Oldsmar Professional Firefighters Local 2980 and on the Pinellas GOP slate; Voter Action Pinellas lists her as a registered Republican. She has about 8-to-1 the resources of her challenger.
raised: $12,497 raised incl. $2,167 in-kind; $5,900 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
backers: Palm Harbor & Oldsmar Professional Firefighters Local 2980; local business/real-estate donors
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat. Voter Action Pinellas (Democratic-aligned) notes she 'has avoided public affiliation with far-right leaders.'
platform: 40-year Palm Harbor resident, Realtor/broker associate for 30+ years, Florida Association of Special Districts certified official (2024 'District Member of the Year'), past chair of Pinellas EMS Advisory Council, Florida Sheriffs Youth Ranches board. Credits her tenure with opening two new fire stations. Says the top issues are Amendment 3 revenue risk (millage capped at 2 mills since 1996; 85% of budget is personnel) and firefighter recruitment/retention; emphasizes reserves for PPE replacement and the district's high-water vehicle for evacuations.
endorsements: Palm Harbor & Oldsmar Professional Firefighters Local 2980; Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate (nonpartisan seat); implied preference of Voter Action Pinellas

name: Elizabeth "Betsey" McKenna
contest: Pinellas Suncoast Fire and Rescue District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. McKenna is the sitting Seat 2 commissioner and current board chair (Indian Rocks Beach representative), on the Pinellas GOP slate; Voter Action Pinellas lists her as a registered Republican and says neither candidate aligns with its values. Both candidates have reported under $1,100, all in-kind. The seat is for the remainder of an unexpired term per local coverage.
raised: $619 in-kind only; $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat.
platform: University of Richmond graduate (Phi Beta Kappa), former insurance field sales manager and business owner; past Indian Rocks Beach budget committee chair and 18-year Calvary Episcopal vestry member. Says she was elected chair during a period of 'upheaval' in the district, restored order to meetings and oversaw hiring a new chief. Touts a budget built on fire assessments and short-term-rental fees rather than ad valorem taxes alone, hardened stations with post-storm communications, cancer insurance and mental-health support for firefighters, and a new CPR training center.
controversy: None reported about McKenna personally; she references a period of administrative turmoil and a chief transition at the district that she says the board resolved.
endorsements: Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate (nonpartisan seat)

name: Daniel Mynsberge
contest: Pinellas Suncoast Fire and Rescue District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Mynsberge, a retired battalion chief and Indian Rocks Beach resident, is challenging the sitting board chair; Voter Action Pinellas lists him as No Party Affiliation. Neither candidate has raised meaningful money. Information is thin.
raised: $1,085 in-kind only; $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record on LGBTQ+ issues; fire-district seat.
platform: Nearly 24 years as a professional firefighter/EMT retiring as battalion chief (recipient of a Medal of Honor and Medal of Merit, apparently in Michigan), then 33 years with American Red Cross Biomedical Services retiring as regional manager of fleet, facilities and logistics; Eagle Scout and CPR instructor. Says the district faces 'growing pains' from building new stations that will need staff and equipment, plus possible Amendment 3 funding cuts; stresses station hardening, forward planning, and better public education about what the district does.

name: Joshua Main
contest: Eastlake Oaks Community Development District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Main is the sitting Seat 2 supervisor (assistant secretary, term expires Nov 2026) on a five-member HOA-scale board for the Eastlake Oaks subdivision in Oldsmar; he appears on the Pinellas GOP slate. Neither candidate has raised or spent any money. Virtually no coverage exists.
raised: $0 raised, $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record; community development district seat.
platform: Current Eastlake Oaks CDD Seat 2 supervisor (listed as 'Josh Main,' assistant secretary) per the district website. No campaign website, bio, or platform found; the seat oversees the subdivision's infrastructure assessments and common areas. Not in the League of Women Voters guide. Voter Action Pinellas lists him as No Party Affiliation, incumbent.
endorsements: Pinellas County Republican Party / Republican Party of Florida slate (nonpartisan seat)

name: J.R. "Nick" Yagnik
contest: Eastlake Oaks Community Development District, Seat 2
pollingDetails: No public poll. Yagnik currently holds Seat 1 on the same CDD board (assistant secretary, term expiring Nov 2026) and is running for Seat 2 against fellow supervisor Joshua Main. Neither candidate has raised or spent money, and there is no press coverage.
raised: $0 raised, $0 spent (Pinellas SOE campaign finance, 2026 cycle, as of Oct 27 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No record; community development district seat.
platform: Sitting Eastlake Oaks CDD Seat 1 supervisor (assistant secretary) per the district website, now seeking Seat 2. No campaign website, bio, or platform found; not in the League of Women Voters guide. Voter Action Pinellas lists him as No Party Affiliation.
